placeFacts.name: Lake Louise
placeFacts.description: Make the lakeshore the main destination, with time for the view before deciding how far to continue.
tips: The designated lakeshore trail is 2.3 km one way. A short lakeshore visit, the whole trail and a teahouse hike are three different plans.

Roam 8X serves the village and lakeshore year-round. A reserved seasonal Parks shuttle starts separately at the ski-resort Park and Ride. Check winter resort transport separately from these lakeshore services.
Use the designated winter lakeshore description. Stay away from the Louise Falls falling-ice area and posted avalanche terrain; a shore route does not require crossing lake ice.

placeFacts.name: Moraine Lake
placeFacts.description: Choose between the Rockpile view, a shoreline outing and an on-site canoe rental, then book a journey that leaves time for that choice.
tips: The Rockpile is a 0.7 km loop with climbing; the lakeshore route is 1.3 km one way. Mountain hikes beyond these are separate commitments.

Moraine Lake Road is closed to personal vehicles year-round, with specific authorised exceptions. Compare reserved Parks transport, permitted commercial services and eligible lodge-guest arrangements.
Ordinary visitor transport is seasonal. The designated winter Moraine Road route ends before large avalanche paths and does not take an ordinary lake visitor to Moraine Lake.

placeFacts.name: Lake Minnewanka
placeFacts.description: A day-use-area view can be the outing, or the start of a separately planned shoreline route.
tips: Reaching Stewart Canyon is different from staying near the day-use area. Its approach includes rough paving, roots and rocks; check the full route profile.
Check seasonal Roam Route 6 or arrange the road journey. A cruise product has its own dates, boarding and return requirements.
Use the permitted road approach and current reports. The western Minnewanka Loop section has a seasonal vehicle closure; do not plan a complete driving loop or infer lake-ice access.

placeFacts.name: Two Jack Lake
placeFacts.description: Build a Banff-based lake pause around the day-use area, with a picnic or a small amount of walking rather than a packed multi-lake circuit.
tips: Choose the actual day-use approach. Campground access and an overnight campsite are separate arrangements from a day visit.
Roam Route 6 is seasonal, including day-use and campground stops. Resolve the actual stop and return; winter requires a different transport plan.
Check the road and shoreline approach. A frozen-looking surface and someone else’s tracks do not establish ice conditions.

placeFacts.name: Johnson Lake
placeFacts.description: Choose a short lakefront pause or investigate the full circuit, leaving enough time for the same journey back to your base.
tips: Parks lists a 2.9 km loop with roots, rocks, step bridges and narrow sections. An easy hiking grade does not establish stroller or wheelchair access.
Check the seasonal Route 6 Johnson Lake stop and final return, or arrange road transport. Bring what the outing needs rather than assuming a lakeside rental or shop.
The summer circuit description does not establish winter footing or ice access. Ask about the actual designated route and current conditions.

placeFacts.name: Vermilion Lakes
placeFacts.description: A town-based viewing plan can leave more time to look and pause, with the return to Banff planned before adding another stop.
tips: Choose a specific public roadside viewing location. Protect wetland vegetation, keep away from wildlife and distinguish a road outing from an informal shoreline path.
Plan the walk, cycle or road journey from your actual starting point. A town-area location does not establish a step-free approach or a reserved parking space.
Check footing and the road approach. Do not use a frozen-water shortcut between viewpoints.

placeFacts.name: Peyto Lake
placeFacts.description: The viewpoint is a distinct objective from reaching the lake shore. Pick the viewpoint plan for a Parkway stop rather than casually extending downhill.
tips: Use the Bow Summit / Peyto viewpoint approach. Parks also lists a separate difficult shore route; it is not the ordinary viewpoint outing.
Arrange the Parkway road journey or the actual tour product, its stop and return. Do not assume that a Lake Louise or Moraine shuttle serves this stop.
Parks publishes a designated winter viewpoint route. Check its map, current snow conditions and the Highway 93N journey; a summer path or parking assumption is insufficient.

placeFacts.name: Bow Lake
placeFacts.description: A lakeside stop and a longer Bow Glacier Falls hike require different time and preparation. Decide which is the objective before leaving your base.
tips: Stay with the chosen designated outing. A lodge or roadside stop does not imply a canoe-rental operation or permission to paddle.
Use Highway 93N conditions and actual tour-stop information. Confirm property access, food and washrooms rather than assuming year-round public services.
Choose a road-access and land-view plan using current reports. Do not extend a summer shoreline description onto lake ice or into avalanche terrain.

placeFacts.name: Herbert Lake
placeFacts.description: Treat a smaller Parkway lake as a chosen stop, with time to park legally and return to the main journey.
tips: Check the day-use access and current report. Smaller scale does not establish easier water conditions or a cleared path.
Arrange the Highway 93N road journey or a product that actually includes this stop. There is no assumed spare space, departure or service in this guide.
Confirm the road and day-use approach before making this the main winter objective. Choose a different stop if the approach or facilities do not fit the group.

placeFacts.name: Fenland Trail
placeFacts.description: A short natural-surface forest loop beside wetland on the edge of Banff townsite.
tips: 1.9 km loop; About 40 min loop estimate. This is the reviewed summer route profile.

Use the designated trailhead and current official route map. Check the trail report, road access and park bulletins before travelling; a published hiking profile does not confirm that the route or parking is available today.
This review covers the summer hiking route. Snow, ice and avalanche terrain require a separate winter route assessment; the summer grade and estimated time are not winter advice.

placeFacts.name: Tunnel Mountain Summit
placeFacts.description: A town-area summit hike with switchbacks, roots and rock, distinct from the campground loop.
tips: 2.3 km one way (published summit profile); About 2 hr estimated return. This is the reviewed summer route profile.

Use the designated trailhead and current official route map. Check the trail report, road access and park bulletins before travelling; a published hiking profile does not confirm that the route or parking is available today.
This review covers the summer hiking route. Snow, ice and avalanche terrain require a separate winter route assessment; the summer grade and estimated time are not winter advice.

placeFacts.name: Stewart Canyon (Lake Minnewanka)
placeFacts.description: A lakeside approach to Stewart Canyon that ends well before the long Aylmer routes.
tips: 1.6 km one way to Stewart Canyon; About 1 hr estimated return. This is the reviewed summer route profile.

Use the designated trailhead and current official route map. Check the trail report, road access and park bulletins before travelling; a published hiking profile does not confirm that the route or parking is available today.
This review covers the summer hiking route. Snow, ice and avalanche terrain require a separate winter route assessment; the summer grade and estimated time are not winter advice.

placeFacts.name: Johnston Canyon Lower Falls
placeFacts.description: A narrow paved canyon path and catwalks to the Lower Falls viewpoint, subject to current access restrictions.
tips: 1.1 km one way (2.2 km return); About 1 hr return. This is the reviewed summer route profile.
Use the Johnston Canyon Day-use Area on the Bow Valley Parkway. Verify the approach road, parking and Route 9 operation for your date; published summer service does not establish winter transport.
Snow and ice can affect paths and catwalks. A traction aid does not override a closure or establish safe access.

placeFacts.name: Lake Agnes
placeFacts.description: A summer mountain hike from Lake Louise to Lake Agnes and a seasonal tea house.
tips: 3.9 km one way (7.8 km return); About 2.5–3 hrs return. This is the reviewed summer route profile.

The trailhead is at Lake Louise lakeshore, separate from the village. Check Roam Route 8X for your date and the seasonal Parks Canada shuttle reservation rules. A bus or parking space does not establish trail access.

Parks Canada identifies avalanche exposure on the Lake Agnes/Mirror Lake and Plain of Six Glaciers summer routes from November to June. These are not ordinary winter walks. Check the official winter route information and avalanche guidance; a summer grade or distance is not a winter recommendation.

placeFacts.name: Bow River (Lake Louise)
placeFacts.description: A village-area riverside route with a choice of sections and a seasonal west-bank restriction.
tips: Up to 5.7 km one way; choose a section; About 2 hr published return estimate; varies with section. This is the reviewed summer route profile.
The west-bank section has a May 15–October 15 seasonal closure. Select a permitted section from the current route map; no complete river loop or winter surface is assumed.
This review covers the summer hiking route. Snow, ice and avalanche terrain require a separate winter route assessment; the summer grade and estimated time are not winter advice.

placeFacts.name: Sunshine Meadows
placeFacts.description: An alpine trail network reached through Sunshine’s seasonal sightseeing operation, with routes crossing the park boundary.
tips: 10.3 km of trails (network, not one loop); 4–5 hr network overview estimate. This is the reviewed summer route profile.

The 10.3 km and 580 m figures belong to the Parks Canada network profile. They do not measure a selected lift-assisted loop or the walk from the base parking area. Use the operator’s map and current operating notice.
This review covers the summer hiking route. Snow, ice and avalanche terrain require a separate winter route assessment; the summer grade and estimated time are not winter advice.

placeFacts.name: Surprise Corner to Hoodoos
placeFacts.description: A natural trail between two separate viewpoints, with ups and downs below the cliffs.
tips: 4.4 km one way; About 3 hr estimated return. This is the reviewed summer route profile.

Use the designated trailhead and current official route map. Check the trail report, road access and park bulletins before travelling; a published hiking profile does not confirm that the route or parking is available today.
This review covers the summer hiking route. Snow, ice and avalanche terrain require a separate winter route assessment; the summer grade and estimated time are not winter advice.

placeFacts.name: Banff Gondola
placeFacts.description: Take the Sulphur Mountain gondola to the summit building and permitted viewing areas.
tips: A single mountain attraction with time inside as well as outdoors.
Check visibility, operation and the Mountain Avenue return. Building access differs from the stair-filled outdoor boardwalk.

placeFacts.name: Ski or Snowboard Lessons
placeFacts.description: Choose instruction for the actual age, discipline and experience before buying overlapping rental or lift products.
tips: A first snow-sport day or a group whose members need different instruction.
Match the school’s meeting point, equipment fitting, supervision and return. Lesson, lift and transport inclusions vary by product.

placeFacts.name: Snow Tubing at Norquay
placeFacts.description: Plan a snow-tube-park visit around the resort’s actual ticket session and participant requirements.
tips: A separate snow activity for a group that is not booking a full ski day.
Check the current age and height rules, footwear, session calendar and return shuttle. A ski ticket does not automatically include tubing.

placeFacts.name: Ice Skating
placeFacts.description: Choose a managed indoor or prepared outdoor skating area, with equipment and session information from its operator.
tips: A short active outing with a planned warm-up and return.
Check the actual rink and rental status. Parks does not monitor natural ice for safety; preparation of one area does not assess a whole lake.

placeFacts.name: Cross-country Skiing
placeFacts.description: Compare designated Nordic routes and classic or skate equipment, with instruction where needed.
tips: A ski-track day that is different from riding resort lifts.
Check grooming, route demands and trail/facility fees. Canmore Nordic Centre needs a separate journey; do not assume a winter local bus reaches it.

placeFacts.name: Cave and Basin
placeFacts.description: Visit exhibitions and permitted thermal-spring viewing areas at the national historic site.
tips: A heritage-focused change of pace from a snow-sport day.
There is no bathing here. Winter hours have closed weekdays and temporary closure blocks; check the actual programme and approach.

placeFacts.name: The Whyte Museum
placeFacts.description: Make art, exhibitions and mountain heritage the main indoor visit at 111 Bear Street.
tips: A cultural town day or an alternative when a mountain outing changes.
Check current exhibitions, admission versus tour tickets and holiday closures. A town-centre address does not settle every access requirement.

placeFacts.name: The Bison Restaurant
placeFacts.description: Choose a seasonal Canadian dinner on Bear Street, then compare the current menu and the table arrangement for your party.
tips: The booking page leaves space for walk-ins and directs groups of 15 or more to its separate events enquiry. Check a dated music or menu event on its own terms.
Use the operator’s Bear Street suite address when arranging the arrival and return.

placeFacts.name: Park Distillery
placeFacts.description: A Banff Avenue restaurant and working distillery with a food menu and separate distillery experiences.
tips: Choose dining, a distillery tour or a private event deliberately; a restaurant table does not include a tour. Check the selected product’s age, booking and service terms.
The restaurant and physical store use 219 Banff Avenue; keep a tour meeting instruction separate from the dining reservation.

placeFacts.name: Wild Flour Bakery
placeFacts.description: A Bear Street bakery and coffee stop with breakfast, sandwiches, soups, salads and pastries on its current operator menu.
tips: Check the current counter selection and menu. Special cake orders use their own advance-order process; ordinary café seating is a separate arrangement.
Use suite 101 on Bear Street, distinct from other venues in the same building.

placeFacts.name: Nourish Bistro
placeFacts.description: A vegetarian and vegan-friendly dining option on Bear Street, with a current operator menu and direct table-booking route.
tips: Discuss the particular ingredients, preparation and dietary needs with the restaurant; a cuisine label is not an allergy-suitability guarantee.
Use suite 110 on Bear Street, distinct from the other restaurants and bakery at 211 Bear Street.

placeFacts.name: Bear Street Tavern
placeFacts.description: A Bear Street option for pizza, sandwiches and pub food, with separate indoor and courtyard seating decisions.
tips: The operator describes a dog-friendly courtyard exposed to the weather. Confirm its actual use and any pet arrangements for your date; group events of 17 or more are directed elsewhere.
Use suite 113 on Bear Street and confirm the entrance or courtyard arrangement you intend to use.

placeFacts.name: BLAKE Brewhouse & Distillery
placeFacts.description: A restaurant, brewhouse and distillery on Bow Valley Trail, with an international-fusion menu and house-produced drinks. Plan the actual Bow Valley Trail address rather than a Main Street pub stop.
tips: The contact page says ordinary restaurant seating is first come, first served. Private functions have a separate enquiry route. Confirm current kitchen service; a late-night menu link does not settle a conflicting hours display.
This is the Bow Valley Trail venue. Do not substitute an old Main Street address or assume these contact and seating rules establish a separate PD3 venue.

placeFacts.name: The Iron Goat Pub & Grill
placeFacts.description: A pub and grill at the Benchlands Trail address, with a published food-and-drink menu and an online reservation route. It is a separate meal journey from Canmore’s Main Street.
tips: The operator links online reservations and asks guests needing immediate assistance to call. Group dining has separate arrangements. Check the current service and confirmation rather than assuming a table or patio.
Use 703 Benchlands Trail for the meal journey, not the imported Main Street address. Arrange the complete return to your accommodation separately.

placeFacts.name: Fairview Bar & Restaurant
placeFacts.description: A restaurant and bar inside Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise with a contemporary Rocky Mountain menu. Plan a lakeside-hotel dining visit, and confirm hotel access and the intended bar or dinner service.
tips: The operator prioritises registered hotel guests and provides a direct dining contact for booking. Confirm access and the specific service; a hotel room or a bar visit does not itself establish a dinner table.
At Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise beside the lake, separate from Lake Louise village and the ski resort. Confirm hotel access before arranging the journey.

placeFacts.name: Fairmont Banff Springs
placeFacts.description: A resort on Spray Avenue, separate from the Banff Avenue town centre. Fairmont currently lists 724 rooms and suites, with main-building and Gatehouse categories. Compare a Fairmont room, a Gatehouse Family Room with bunk beds, or an accessible category before selecting the exact layout.
tips: Room location, bunk layout and mobility features vary by category. Local transit passes do not establish ski-shuttle coverage. Confirm current pool/spa access, room facilities and any additional charges for the actual stay.
Confirm the exact room, total price, access requirements and cancellation conditions directly before booking.

placeFacts.name: Moose Hotel and Suites
placeFacts.description: A Banff Avenue hotel with hotel rooms and one- or two-bedroom suites. Suites have a kitchen nook rather than a full cooking kitchen. The property lists two rooftop hot pools, an indoor pool, Meadow Spa and Pacini Italian Restaurant.
tips: The official site lists kitchen nooks in suites, not full kitchens. Local Roam guest passes cover Banff local services; the hotel FAQ says Lake Louise and Johnston Canyon services cost extra. Check your specific winter transfer separately.
Confirm the exact room, total price, access requirements and cancellation conditions directly before booking.

placeFacts.name: Banff Park Lodge
placeFacts.description: A Lynx Street hotel near central Banff with Standard and Superior rooms, plus several distinct suite categories. Standard Rooms are advertised with no view; selected Superior Rooms have roll-in showers. The operator currently reports ongoing lobby and public-space renovations.
tips: Checked 29 October 2026: the home page reports ongoing lobby/public renovations and the guest directory lists La Terrazza closed. Pool, restaurant and access arrangements should be reconfirmed. Parking is not guaranteed; ask about the actual ski-shuttle stop and airport transfer.
Confirm the exact room, total price, access requirements and cancellation conditions directly before booking.

placeFacts.name: HI Banff Alpine Centre
placeFacts.description: A hostel at 801 Hidden Ridge Way on Tunnel Mountain, with shared four-to-six-bed rooms and several private categories. A shared kitchen, Cougar Pete’s restaurant and local bus passes offer different meal and transport choices. Select the actual bathroom arrangement: an ensuite WC is not the same description as a private ensuite room.
tips: HI’s local bus pass is a town-transport benefit, not evidence of an airport or ski-resort transfer. Confirm the stop, evening service and the exact room’s bathroom before booking.
Confirm the exact room, total price, access requirements and cancellation conditions directly before booking.

placeFacts.name: Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise
placeFacts.description: A hotel at the Lake Louise lakeshore in Banff National Park, with standard, lakeview and Fairmont Gold room categories. It is separate from the village and Lake Louise Ski Resort. Choose the specific room view and check the terms for wellness and seasonal activities.
tips: The dining page restricts the hotel and food-and-beverage outlets to registered overnight guests on 26–29 October 2026. This is a dated notice. The rental shop page was awaiting the 2026/27 reopening at review. Confirm current access, skating and rental operation rather than assuming a room includes every activity.
Confirm the exact room, total price, access requirements and cancellation conditions directly before booking.

placeFacts.name: Lake Louise Inn
placeFacts.description: A Lake Louise village property with hotel rooms and condo-style accommodation across several buildings. Some categories have kitchens. The official site lists an indoor pool, whirlpools, three dining venues and a winter shuttle connection to Lake Louise Ski Resort.
tips: Some accommodation is in walk-up buildings; do not assume all rooms have elevator access. The hotel advertises a complimentary winter ski shuttle, but the resort had not yet posted the coming winter’s pickup details at review. Confirm the actual outbound and return before booking lessons.
Confirm the exact room, total price, access requirements and cancellation conditions directly before booking.

placeFacts.name: The Malcolm Hotel
placeFacts.description: A hotel at 321 Spring Creek Drive in Canmore, with a rooftop outdoor pool and hot tubs. Room categories differ in outlook, balcony, bathing fixtures and pet eligibility. The Premium Double Queen has a wet bar and mini-fridge, not a full kitchen; compare it with a condo-style stay when cooking is a priority.
tips: Checked 29 October 2026: the hotel publishes nearby construction of the future Alexander Boutique Hotel & Spa and asks guests to discuss impacts. Outdoor pool/hot-tub operation is weather-dependent; do not infer availability from the amenity listing.
Confirm the exact room, total price, access requirements and cancellation conditions directly before booking.

placeFacts.name: Coast Canmore Hotel & Conference Centre
placeFacts.description: A Bow Valley Trail hotel at 511 Bow Valley Trail in Canmore, with an indoor pool, hot tub and Table Food + Drink. Standard, patio, accessible and Premium King Suite categories have different equipment. Parking is currently paid and first come, first served, so include it when comparing this base with downtown or condo options.
tips: Official services list paid parking; the old free-parking claim is removed. The published airporter option requires its own booking and does not establish ski-resort or lake transport.
Confirm the exact room, total price, access requirements and cancellation conditions directly before booking.

placeFacts.name: Banff Visitor Centre
placeFacts.description: Start with official visitor information for routes, park rules and current planning questions.
tips: Check the official location, opening details and available service before travelling.

placeFacts.name: Lake Louise Visitor Centre
placeFacts.description: Ask about the actual Lake Louise outing, current reports and the journey between village, lakeshore and resort.
tips: Check the official location, opening details and available service before travelling.
